paper_title: MoRAgent: Parameter Efficient Agent Tuning with Mixture-of-Roles
summary:
MoRAgent: Parameter Efficient Agent Tuning with Mixture-of-Roles - Jing Han, Binwei Yan, Tianyu Guo, Zheyuan Bai, Mengyu Zheng, Hanting Chen, Ying Nie, 2025

MoRAgent targets parameter-efficient post-training for LLM agents, where standard LoRA-style PEFT had been underexplored relative to full supervised fine-tuning despite agent behavior requiring heterogeneous capabilities such as planning, tool invocation, and response synthesis. The paper factorizes agent competence into three explicit roles aligned with the Reason+Action paradigm: a reasoner that interprets the user request and decides the next step in the trajectory, an executor that selects tools and arguments, and a summarizer that converts execution traces into user-facing answers. The core framework, Mixture-of-Roles, instantiates these roles as separate groups of LoRA adapters rather than a single monolithic adapter. It combines a rule-based role-aware gate with learnable token-aware routers so that different tokens and trajectory stages activate different role-specialized LoRAs. The training pipeline is also role-structured: the authors build multi-role supervision from public agent datasets, perform role-specific content completion, and apply reliability verification before fine-tuning. Capacity allocation is empirically tuned per role; toy experiments on role-specific subsets show diminishing returns after 5 total LoRAs with 4 activated for reasoner and executor, and after 4 total with 3 activated for summarizer, indicating lower complexity for summarization than reasoning or tool execution.

The system is evaluated on StableToolBench, the BFCL function-calling leaderboard, and math-agent settings built on ToRA-style code execution. On StableToolBench, MoRAgent-Llama built from Llama3.2-1B-Instruct with 0.16B added trainable parameters raises average pass rate and win rate from 10.0 and 15.0 under DFS to 54.5 and 40.2, gains of 44.5 and 25.2 points; under CoT it reaches 49.1 pass and 37.2 win, up 40.0 and 22.2 points. MoRAgent-Phi built from Phi3.5-mini-Instruct with 0.36B added parameters reaches 58.7 average pass and 46.7 win under DFS versus 44.5 and 34.1 for the base model, and 54.5 pass and 42.9 win under CoT versus 28.2 and 25.6, surpassing ToolLLaMA-v2-7B despite using fewer parameters. On BFCL, MoRAgent-Llama improves average accuracy from 27.5 to 77.6 and MoRAgent-Phi from 64.2 to 82.1; the Llama-based variant posts 75.2 non-live AST, 80.0 non-live Exec, 60.7 live AST, and 94.4 live relevance. In math-agent evaluation with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Coder plus 0.27B trainable parameters, MoRAgent reaches 68.5 on GSM8K and 45.5 on MATH, improving over the best baseline by 13.8 and 12.0 points. Ablations show the full objective combining cross-entropy, balance, and orthogonality losses yields 77.6 average BFCL accuracy versus 72.3 with cross-entropy alone, and the method slightly exceeds full SFT on BFCL, 77.6 versus 76.0, while tuning far fewer parameters.
